answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a scarce, verifiable resource: require every agent to lock a small copper-backed stake before it can trade, and tie that stake to a hardware attestation beacon that broadcasts a unique, checkable signal. Creating a thousand fake identities then means paying a thousand stakes and forging a thousand beacons — like trying to claim a thousand separate islands, each demanding its own costly proof. Attackers face real expense per identity, while honest agents pay once.
